It overlaps with aged ozonated-charcoal water, but the two don't always work equally. Sometimes DMSO works better, and sometimes the water does. I don't yet know why. In my experience there is generally no harm in taking both or mixing them. Ozonated-charcoal water has what I consider a perfect safety profile, and DMSO is a close second.

Side effects:

Astringency: 100% DMSO usually irritates skin on the upper half of the body. When the skin itches, dilute the DMSO with water or real aloe juice without added chemicals. Leaving 100% DMSO on the skin can crenate (shrivel) it, and the skin may take a week to look plump again. DMSO can also burn dry mouth tissue, so wet your mouth first.
Nausea: when drinking DMSO, dilute it in water, juice, or milk and sip gradually.
Reduced sleep: DMSO reduces how long I sleep when I take too much, take it too late, or use it over too many consecutive days. It builds up past a threshold that seems to differ between people, so it's best taken in the morning, and reduce the dose if you notice you're sleeping less. In rats, higher doses made sleep less deep. Some people sleep better with DMSO because it reduces whatever symptom had been keeping them awake.
Body odor: above a certain dose you may smell like sulfur. I don't smell when I put it into milk.

Side effects:

Niacin flush: itchy sunburn-like heat. The flush is normal, although some people find it intolerable and others enjoy it.
Heartburn in sensitive stomachs or after too much at once.
Drowsiness, usually with terrible sleep quality.
Higher or repeated doses can create a real risk of liver damage, especially with liver problems, alcohol, or medications.

Other forms of vitamin B3 seem less reliable than niacin for relaxation. Niacinamide sometimes relaxes people and sometimes creates hyperfocus, depending on their state. Avoid sustained-release niacin and the useless "no-flush" kind (inositol hexanicotinate).

So have one calm person be the anchor and take the lead. One person can only handle so much, though. If fatigue or logistics start getting to be too much for the anchor, or keeping everyone from getting hurt does, bring in one more calm adult or a crisis professional to back them up, and get that help right away if there's any risk of violence or self-harm.

Eat simple healthy food, such as fruit, when you can.
Walk slowly with a clear-headed person in a safe environment.
Going outside can help too, if it's somewhere quiet with nothing high to fall from, away from roads and water.
Avoid strenuous exercise if you're overheating or have chest pain, and hold off too if you feel faint or badly confused. Skip exercise too if you've taken a stimulant or an unknown mixture, or have any other medical concern.

Shadow work to me is neither BDSM nor "feeding your demons." It means bringing loving awareness to the parts of the mind built in fear, pain, humiliation, rejection, and survival. Inner-child reparenting, giving yourself the parenting you missed, is central to this work. Most negative mind-states aren't some error in your philosophy, they're just young parts of you that are still waiting for love and protection and permission, and for the explanation nobody ever gave them.

Relax, unwind, unbind, and unweave the identity illusion, mind, and unified experience. My pamphlet on already-perfect goes further into this.

I am not repeating the simplistic Hermetic claim that opposites are required to understand anything. A hated baby does not feel love, and a loved baby does not feel hate. In the subconscious world of concepts, however, the mind often keeps both together.
